B: the empty back wall and isolated floor light spots have no useful hierarchy.

B: large bare floor and back wall remain uncomposed.

highest_value_fixes.fix: Rebuild night value hierarchy: retain dark cool stone/wood between localized warm fixtures, reduce the uniform tan atmospheric veil, connect floor illumination to visible sources and establish foot/prop contact shading. Keep signage and shrine forms visible without washing the whole room.

Author a structural rhythm using coherent supports, thresholds and intentional window bays; resolve cut-off far windows and indoor exterior-like eaves. Group useful furnishings at a reception/rest function with purposeful negative space and a quieter floor instead of a vast repeated cobble field.

Supply or adapt purpose-built shrine pedestals and portal/biome insignia: thick sculptural bases, relic-bearing horizontal crowns, readable symbols integrated into stone/timber. Current repeated lecterns and tiny text strips cannot carry the landmark identity through lighting alone. This is a silhouette/art need, not necessarily a purchase or generation request.

bar_a_world_fit_rationale: No for either arm at the requested complete bar. Stone, timber, teal cloth and the blue-shirted expedition trainer share broad Meadows vocabulary. A has a more inviting human use story than B. However the keyart has designed massing, strong value/depth grouping and coherent warm/cool mood; these captures are repetitive flat interior shells by day and beige veils at night. This judgment is about palette, mood, composition and silhouette, not painted pixel fidelity.
bar_b_atmosphere_rationale: No for either arm. The trainer and medieval fantasy subject matter plausibly suggest the broad genre, but the actual presentation does not yet feel like the same finished kind of game as the supplied Palworld scenes: material hierarchy, grounded subjects, convincing lit space and spatial storytelling fall short. Night lighting particularly misses the written Valheim-class localized-light/cool-depth target. No Valheim image was supplied, so that component uses ART_DIRECTION prose.

whole_sheet_scores.method: Equal-weight arithmetic mean of all 26 separately reviewed camera/preset entries; 0-10.

verdict: A is preferred over B throughout for visible human-use furnishings, especially the nave endpoint and candle-dressed shrine. The improvement is real but modest and does not resolve the core defect: neither arm yet reads as sufficiently authored, coherent, inhabited architecture with convincing character integration at shipping quality. Keep this Hall interior criterion open.
evidence_notes: Viewed the contact sheet first, all five supplied Palworld images and Meadows keyart, then all 52 full-size images representing 26 A/B pairs. No source, mapping, receipts, other judges or prior scores inspected.

Medium and High were inspected as separate observations. High has slightly stronger local grounding around some wall/floor joins in day views, but it does not change the principal defects or warrant a score-band increase; matching scores are intentional.

Small-size: trainer silhouette and portal openings remain readable; signage, bench use and shrine function do not. Night washes furnishings into background while black windows remain disproportionately salient.

Character art plainly: tousled brown hair, blue shirt, pale collar, tan backpack and dark trousers form an appealing readable adventurer silhouette. Fine texture is noisy at this size, rear-only pose prevents face evaluation, and dark crisp character versus washed room plus weak contact creates a hovering/cutout impression. Fixed idle is disclosed; no animation conclusion is made.

Scale: using the disclosed 1.80m trainer, benches and desk suggest broadly usable human scale, door height is generous but plausible for a civic hall, and nave height is plausible. Immense undivided floor and uniform high window bands weaken perceived scale; shrine stands read near human height as lecterns rather than substantial display architecture. No numeric world dimensions inferred.
Rain interior is distinguishable mostly by darker grade, not strong source-driven weather mood. This is an interior-only observation and does not judge exterior rain effects.
No performance, full-world, traversal, exterior or continuous motion acceptance is inferred.

yes_no.qualification: Answers concern the full requested visual bar, not whether generic medieval fantasy subject matter is compatible.
